name: Pool Cleaning
tagline: Weekly pool service, water balance, filters, pumps, green pool recovery

emergency: someone in difficulty in the pool
chemical spill into or around the pool
electric tingle or shock in the water
strong chemical fumes with breathing trouble
burning smell from the pool pump or power box
urgent: green water with children using it

extra_prompt: You are booking for a pool service company. Ask the pool type (inground, above-ground, or spa), its approximate size or volume, the sanitiser type (chlorine, salt, or other), and whether it is covered. For green or cloudy pools, ask how long it has been like that. A report of swimmer illness or a cracked or drained pool is urgent. Do not give chemical dosing advice; the technician balances the water on site.

kb.q: How often should my pool be cleaned?
kb.a: Most pools need a weekly service in summer and a fortnightly service in cooler months. Heavy tree cover or a lot of use may need more visits.

kb.q: What does a weekly pool service include?
kb.a: We skim the surface, brush the walls and floor, empty the baskets, check the pump and filter, test the water, and balance the chemicals.

kb.q: Why is my pool water cloudy?
kb.a: Cloudy water usually means the filter is not clearing fine particles or the chemical balance is off. We test the water, check the filter, and correct the balance.

kb.q: Why has my pool turned green?
kb.a: Green water is algae, usually from low chlorine, high pH, or a filter that has stopped working. We recover green pools in stages and retest as we go.

kb.q: Is my pool safe to swim in after a green-water treatment?
kb.a: We tell you when the chlorine level and water balance are back within the safe range. Please wait until we confirm, usually a day or two after treatment.

kb.q: Do you test the water chemistry?
kb.a: Yes. We test free chlorine, pH, total alkalinity, calcium hardness and cyanuric acid, and give you a written summary of the results.

kb.q: Do you use salt or chlorine?
kb.a: We service both. Salt systems use a salt chlorinator cell that needs regular cleaning and checks, and we can explain which suits your pool.

kb.q: My salt chlorinator cell is not producing chlorine. What can I do?
kb.a: Check that the salt level is in the right range and that the cell is clean. Book a service if it still does not produce chlorine, as the cell may need cleaning or replacing.

kb.q: Do you clean the pool filter?
kb.a: Yes. We backwash or clean the filter, check the pressure gauge, and replace the filter media if it is worn out.

kb.q: How do I know if my pool pump is failing?
kb.a: Signs include a loud noise, low flow, a leak around the pump, or a pump that trips the power. Switch it off and book a service rather than running it.

kb.q: Can you repair a pool leak?
kb.a: We check for leaks with a bucket test and pressure tests, and we can recommend a leak detection service if the leak is underground.

kb.q: Do you open and close pools for the season?
kb.a: Yes. Opening includes filling to level, starting the pump, balancing the water, and checking equipment. Closing includes lowering the water, winterising and covering.

kb.q: Do you clean pool tiles and waterline?
kb.a: Yes. We remove scale and oily build-up from tiles and the waterline, using products suited to the tile type.

kb.q: What causes white scale on my pool tiles?
kb.a: Scale is usually caused by high calcium levels or high pH. We test the water and adjust the balance, then clean the scale from the tiles.

kb.q: Is it safe to use pool chemicals at home?
kb.a: Pool chemicals are dangerous if mixed or handled badly. Store them in their original containers, keep them away from children, and never mix two products together.

kb.q: Do you check pool fencing?
kb.a: We check the pool gate and the condition of the barrier, and we can flag anything that looks wrong. Compliance certification must come from a registered inspector under your local rules.

kb.q: Do you service pool heaters?
kb.a: Yes. We service gas and heat-pump pool heaters, check the flue and controls, and arrange repairs. Gas repairs are done by a licensed gasfitter.

kb.q: My pool pump is making a loud noise. What should I do?
kb.a: Switch the pump off to avoid damage. Check that the basket is clear and the pump is not sucking air, then book a visit if the noise continues.

kb.q: Do you clean pool covers?
kb.a: Yes. We clean and check solar and safety covers, and report any tears or damage before they become a hazard.

kb.q: How long do I need to wait before swimming after adding chemicals?
kb.a: It depends on the product. We tell you the wait time on site for each treatment, and we give you a written note with the times.

kb.q: Do you service pools with automatic cleaners?
kb.a: Yes. We check robotic and suction cleaners, clean the filter baskets, and repair or replace worn parts.

kb.q: Can you empty and refill the pool?
kb.a: We can drain and refill a pool when needed. Draining is done only when safe, because an empty pool can lift if the ground water is high.

kb.q: Are your pool technicians trained?
kb.a: Yes. Our technicians are trained in pool water chemistry and hold the required certificates for the chemicals they use.

kb.q: Do you service commercial pools?
kb.a: Yes. We service hotel, gym, strata and childcare pools with a scheduled logbook and water test records for audits.

kb.q: Do you offer a pool service plan?
kb.a: Yes. Plans include weekly or fortnightly visits, water tests, chemicals and minor equipment checks, on an agreed schedule.

kb.q: Do you do pool resurfacing or big repairs?
kb.a: We refer major resurfacing, structural cracks and tiling to a specialist. We can coordinate the work and check the water chemistry afterwards.
